title: How Oliver Brocato built TABS Chocolate for virality: creator networks, hybrid pay, diversified channels
summary: Oliver Brocato explains why he designed TABS around short-form virality instead of marketing an existing product. He covers scaling with many creator-run pages, moving to hybrid retainer plus revenue share, diversifying channels, using packaging for first purchase, and using a personal brand for hiring and networking.

principles.text: Design the product to go viral itself instead of trying to market an existing product.
principles.quote: I want to build a product that can go viral by itself and so you know that's what tabs is

principles.text: Make the product instantly understandable in a few seconds so short-form creators can demo it easily.
principles.quote: you're able to kind of understand how it works in like a 3 second like snippet or sound bite

principles.text: Scale creator content horizontally: many creators, each running their own independent brand page, rather than stacking creators on one page.
principles.quote: instead of bringing on more content creators adding them to the page I expanded horizontally bringing on as many creators as I possibly could and setting them up with their own independent page

principles.text: Pay creators a small retainer plus a percentage of upside, since pure affiliate is hard to recruit for.
principles.quote: a hybrid of like super small retainer enough where like they're happy if nothing happens yeah um but you know not a crazy amount of money and then giving them a percentage of all the upside

principles.text: Avoid reliance on one channel; build many channels so small incremental lifts compound.
principles.quote: instead of being over reliant on one channel when you're like an octopus and you have your tentacles on 12 different channels

principles.text: Packaging wins the first purchase, but product quality drives repeat orders and word of mouth.
principles.quote: the packaging is what gets us to acquire the first customer now if the product isn't good the customer is not coming back
